summary.text: The Storming of the Bastille happened in Paris on 14 July 1789, when revolutionary insurgents attacked and seized a medieval armoury, fortress and political prison.
The Bastille represented royal authority in the centre of Paris, and revolutionaries saw it as a symbol of the monarchy's abuse of power.
Its fall was the flashpoint of the French Revolution, and France marks 14 July with a national holiday.

facts.label: Holiday
facts.value: 14 July, called Bastille Day in English

items.prompt: The Bastille held only seven inmates and was already due for demolition. Why did revolutionaries still attack it?

options.label: They wanted to free thousands of political prisoners inside
They saw it as a symbol of the monarchy's abuse of power
They planned to turn it into the seat of a new assembly
They believed the king himself was hiding behind its walls

items.explain: The Bastille represented royal authority, and the revolutionaries saw it as a symbol of the monarchy's abuse of power.

items.prompt: What did Louis XVI do just before the storming that angered Paris?

options.label: He dismissed and banished Necker, who had been sympathetic to the Third Estate, and replaced the ministry
He ordered the Third Estate to leave Versailles and end its meetings
He closed the Palais-Royal and ordered its crowds to be dispersed
He named a new governor for the Bastille and ordered it demolished

items.explain: On 11 July, under the influence of conservative nobles, the king dismissed Necker and completely reconstituted the ministry.

items.prompt: The officers of the French Guards failed to rally their men. What did the rebellious citizens gain from that?

options.label: A large store of cannons and food
The loyalty of the king's ministers
A trained military contingent
The command of the royal cavalry

items.explain: The Guards, who were favourably disposed to the popular cause, could not be rallied, so the citizens acquired a trained military contingent.

items.prompt: What combination worsened France's economic crisis in the years before the Bastille fell?

options.label: The cost of a long civil war, high tariffs and overseas trade
The loss of colonial income, a bank failure and new fines
The cost of building palaces, a cattle disease and war debts
The cost of intervening in the American Revolution, regressive taxes and poor harvests

items.explain: The crisis was caused in part by the cost of intervening in the American Revolution and made worse by regressive taxes and poor harvests.

items.prompt: Held back by old protocols, the commoners' representatives broke away and formed their own body. What was its purpose?

options.label: To end the monarchy at once
To create a French constitution
To raise a militia for Paris
To put the governor on trial

items.explain: The Third Estate reconstituted itself as the National Assembly, a body whose purpose was the creation of a French constitution.

items.prompt: France celebrates a national holiday each 14 July. What does it commemorate?

options.label: The execution of Louis XVI and the founding of the First Republic
The meeting of the Estates General and the National Assembly's first vote
The storming of the Bastille and the Fête de la Fédération on its first anniversary
The end of the Reign of Terror and the coup of 18 Brumaire

items.explain: The holiday commemorates the storming of the Bastille and the Fête de la Fédération held on its first anniversary in 1790.
